newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER-MONACO MUST BE AT THEIR BEST TO OVERCOME INTER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO MUST BE AT THEIR BEST TO OVERCOME INTER.

text.p: Monaco must return to their best form if they are to overcome Internazionale in the second leg of their UEFA Cup semifinal on Tuesday.
The French champions-elect, who had won all their previous away legs in this season's competition, played poorly and lost 3-1 in the first leg in Milan two weeks ago.

And as French international defender Patrick Blondeau said on Monday: "What we have to prove to everyone is that we're a great team by turning round an unfavourable result, something we haven't had to do this season."

Monaco, on the verge of their sixth French league title, found their game in the second half in Milan and scored what could prove to be a crucial goal through unsettled Nigerian striker Victor Ikpeba, their top scorer with six goals in the competition.

Their difficulties continued with a 2-0 league defeat at Bordeaux last week, in which Ikpeba was on from the start, and the tension at their training camp in the mountains behind the principality has been palpable.

But coach Jean Tigana and his players have worked hard at concentrating their minds on the tough task on Tuesday when they must pull back two goals to stand any chance of reaching their second European final following a losing appearance in the 1992 European Cup Winners Cup to Germans Werder Bremen.

"The objective from the start is to not concede a goal and to attack as much as possible," Tigana said. "We've got to manage to score in the first half in order to not make the situation even more difficult for ourselves."
Tigana will rely on veteran Enzo Scifo, who returns to his first club Anderlecht in his native Belgium at the end of the season, to dictate play against another of his former clubs.

Inter, whose stated priority is one of Italy's two European Cup berths next season but whose best chance of a trophy is the UEFA Cup, will look to close all the gaps in defence to avoid conceding the early goal Monaco are after.
A favourable combination of weekend league results has left Inter feeling ultra-confident.

Inter were boosted not only by a 2-1 away win against Cagliari on Saturday but also by Udinese's 2-0 defeat of Parma which left them third in Serie A with just six games to play and a place in next season's Champions League a possibility.
Inter's experienced captain Giuseppe Bergomi said: "It was a big boost for us to win at Cagliari where no side, not even Juventus, had won for six months.
"I've always said that I'd prefer to finish second in the league rather than win the UEFA Cup and therefore Parma's defeat was good news for us."

Bergomi, striker Maurizio Ganz, Swiss midfielder Ciriaco Sforza, French schemer Youri Djorkaeff and defender Salvatore Fresi did not play against Cagliari on Saturday, all being rested for Tuesday's cup tie.
With the exception of Chilean striker Ivan Zamorano and defender Alessandro Pistone, both suspended, Inter's English coach Roy Hodgson has a full squad at his disposal.
Monaco: Fabien Barthez; Patrick Blondeau, Franck Dumas, Martin Djetou, Emmanuel Petit; Sylvain Legwinski, John Collins, Enzo Scifo; Victor Ikpeba, Sonny Anderson, Thierry Henry.
Internazionale: Gianluca Pagliuca; Jocelyn Angloma, Salvatore Fresi, Massimo Paganin, Giuseppe Bergomi; Javier Zanetti, Ciriaco Sforza, Paul Ince; Youri Djorkaeff, Marco Branca, Maurizio Ganz.
